unified-diff.description: A unified patch, either as one text value or as a file manifest whose patch fields Leaf delivers separately on demand.

lf-diff.description:
A unified diff rendered by Pierre with native per-file collapse, file filtering, durable reviewed marks, next-unreviewed navigation, old/new line numbers, full add/delete line backgrounds, brighter inline word changes, visible but unselectable +/− indicators, and per-file +/− counts. Line numbers and indicators stay outside copied and commented source text. A reviewed mark is an explicit reader action folded by file path; filtering is temporary and never hides files from print or export. Add `collapsed` when every file should start closed, especially for a large patch; a comment or navigation target still opens the containing file and clears a filter that hid it. Bind `source` to a page-owned unified-diff feed and use `snapshot` for an immutable capture; each rendered line then becomes a commentable datum keyed by file path, old/new side, and source line. The feed may hold patch text or, for large reviews, a `files` manifest whose path-keyed `patch` fields Leaf delivers only when their files open. The bound form is `
`; the empty `
` preserves the shared data-body shape and its content is ignored. With no source, the diff verbatim inside its 
, at column 0, remains the authored fallback. Every changed file needs at least one `@@` hunk header, whose old and new counts must match the following lines exactly. A path-only rename is the only supported hunkless entry and appears as one old → new row; write that block as exactly four lines: `diff --git`, `similarity index 100%`, `rename from`, and `rename to`, with the same non-empty old and new paths in the header and rename lines. A rename with changes uses the normal disclosure labeled with its new path. Binary, mode-only, empty added/deleted, and copy entries are unsupported, so state those changes in prose rather than mixing them into the diff; for an edited copy destination, omit the copy metadata and provide its textual hunks. Context lines keep their leading space; encode a context line with nothing after that prefix as   so HTML parsing preserves it. HTML-escape an inline body — & as & first, then < and > as < and > — or a diff whose lines carry entity text (& in source, say) is silently altered before rendering. Comments anchor to the required id. Takes no language: each file's own path is read for one ($languages), so keep the `diff --git` or ---/+++ headers rather than pasting bare hunks, and a path naming no language leaves that file plain.
lf-diff.x-example:
diff --git a/feeders/mount.py b/feeders/mount.py
--- a/feeders/mount.py
+++ b/feeders/mount.py
@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@
 def bracket():
-    return "plastic"
+    return "steel"
